name: syncthing
description: Private peer-to-peer file synchronization with a browser-based interface

fields.name: SYNCTHING_WEBUI_PORT
fields.label: R1: Web UI Port
fields.help:
Host port used to open the Syncthing Web UI.
Important: After first login, immediately open Actions > Settings and configure a Web UI username and password. Syncthing initially listens on all interfaces without Web UI credentials.

fields.name: SYNCTHING_LISTEN_PORT
fields.label: R2: Synchronization Port
fields.help: Host port used for Syncthing device connections over both TCP and UDP. It maps to Syncthing's internal port 22000.

fields.name: SYNCTHING_DISCOVERY_PORT
fields.label: R3: Local Discovery Port
fields.help: UDP port used to discover other Syncthing devices on the local network. Keep the default unless you have a specific reason to change it.

fields.name: CONFIG_LOCATION
fields.label: R4: Config Folder
fields.help: Host folder for Syncthing configuration, device identity, certificates, and application state.

fields.name: DATA_1_LOCATION
fields.label: R5: Primary Sync Folder
fields.help:
Primary host folder made available to Syncthing at /data1.
Adding the mount does not automatically create a Syncthing folder; select /data1 when configuring a shared folder in the Web UI.

fields.name: PUID
fields.label: R6: PUID
fields.help: Linux user ID used by the container. This account must have permission to read and write the selected sync folders.

fields.name: PGID
fields.label: R7: PGID
fields.help: Linux group ID used by the container for bind-mounted file permissions.

fields.name: TZ
fields.label: R8: Timezone
fields.help: Timezone used by Syncthing, such as Asia/Dubai or Etc/UTC.

fields.name: SYNCTHING_HOSTNAME
fields.label: O1: Device Hostname
fields.help: Optional hostname used by the container. This can help identify the device in Syncthing. Clear it to let Docker assign the hostname.

fields.name: DATA_2_MOUNT
fields.label: O2: Additional Sync Folder
fields.help:
Optional second full bind mount.
Example: /volume2/family:/data2.
Syncthing will see this folder at /data2. Leave blank to omit it, then select /data2 when configuring the folder in Syncthing.

fields.name: RESTART_POLICY
fields.label: O3: Restart Policy
fields.help: Controls whether the container restarts automatically.

fields.name: SYNCTHING_NETWORK_MODE
fields.label: O4: Network
fields.help:
Choose Create New Bridge for the default Compose network, Host Mode for host networking, or an existing named Docker network.
Host mode can improve local discovery but exposes Syncthing directly on the NAS network, so secure the Web UI immediately.

fields.name: SYNCTHING_IMAGE
fields.label: A1: Image
fields.help: Official LinuxServer Syncthing image. Change this only if you need a different image tag.

fields.name: SYNCTHING_CONTAINER_NAME
fields.label: Container Name
fields.help: EasyDocker sets the container name from the project name.

fields.name: SYNCTHING_LISTEN_INTERNAL_PORT
fields.label: Internal Synchronization Port
fields.help: Recipe-managed internal TCP and UDP synchronization port.

ui.overview: Syncthing synchronizes folders directly between trusted devices without storing your data in a central cloud service.
what_happens: One Syncthing container will be created using the LinuxServer image
Configuration and sync data will be stored in bind-mounted host folders
TCP and UDP synchronization traffic will use port 22000 by default
Local device discovery will use UDP port 21027
You must add the mounted data paths as folders inside the Syncthing Web UI
Set a Web UI username and password immediately after deployment because the initial interface has no credentials
The container will use the selected Docker networking mode
ui.data_location: Each storage field can be relative to this app's config folder or an absolute host path. Ensure the selected PUID and PGID can read and write every synchronized folder.
